title: Playing with Rene Parker, then leading his own band
summary: Two years with Rene Parker's band in St. Bernard Parish, then his own band with Albert Walters, Frank Crump and Elwood Theodore for about three years.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Very well. There, it's going again the machine stopped for a second. We were talking about Celestan and can you think of anything else that you went on from there after that group? After that group?

Well, I started playing with René Parker, a trumpet player. A fella, him and Big Fire, they call him, trombone player. They made up a band and they was going down the country, the Burris and all down in St. Bernard Parish. Mostly, that's the most of their work were down there playing. So, I got with that band. It was called Onida Jazz Band. And I drifted right along with them playing. I must have stayed with them about two years. The job was pretty good. And I did alright with them. And then I came back and thought that I could organize my own band.
Yeah, we're having trouble with this recorder now, but we'll try to finish up quickly so we'll get the rest of your life in here within five minutes if we can.

And I decided that I would make up a band of my own and I would be the manager of the band. So, I made up a band with Albert Walters, Frank Crump, Elwood Theodore. And we went along playing and doing nicely. And we must have stood together about three years. And finally, I meets up with Albert Boybanks, who I played with often and on. But Albert Boybanks made up a band and we begin to get together and play. And then out of Blue Sky one day, I meets a man they call Mr. Russell. And we're about that time that I came in here to hear you. Together, man. And we recorded some numbers from him. Can you recall the numbers?
